Instead, you are scored based not only on how many points you score legitimately, but also on how many points you concede through foul shots, and how many shots you take in total. You always take the next shot, even if you've missed or fouled, so in a one player game the break-building strategies can be slightly more aggressive than in a real match, as there's no risk of leaving an opponent a chance

As in the real game you start off by trying to pot a red (there are 10 or the real 15, depending on which mode you choose), and if successful choosing one of the 6 colours (by pressing the number corresponding to its points value). Once you've lined up the direction of the shot, you will have to set the speed, and then the spin.

218288.overview: Computer Scrabble is the earliest official computer version of the popular word game. The game has a 8500-20000 word dictionary depending on the computer, containing the most frequently-used words in Scrabble. As a result, some very obscure words (mostly of 2 and 3 letters - keen Scrabble players will know that these are often the most profitable scoring method) are included, but common words such as 'bigot' and 'sheen' are queried by the game - simply tell it that your move is a word and it will move on trustingly. Inputting words is done by moving the cursor across or down to the starting position of the word, and then pressing to key the word in, pressing space before the letter you wish to use a blank tile as. All words formed are accurately scored. The game can juggle your tiles and allow you to manually rearrange them, and you can watch the computer 'think' as it notices possible moves and their scoring. There are four difficulty levels, with the highest capable of combined scores over 700.

218293.overview:
Wicked Jack Frost has stolen some of Santa's presents on Christmas Eve and taken them to his secret cave. You are Santa's assistant and have to recover them, however Jack's cave is protected by Abominable Snowmen, and evil stinging bats, also blocks of snow and ice keep falling from the roof.

When you are past these obstacles and have retrieved the presents, you take them back to Santa by the same route.. but you can only carry five presents per journey, so several dangerous trips are needed to make sire everyone gets their Christmas presents on time.

218294.overview:
Snake Pit is a fast-paced game where the player controls a character shaped like a grinning face. The goal is to eat up all the eggs that fill up the single screen field entirely and survive as long as possible to reach the next stage. Also in the field are multiple snakes with a different colour. They cannot escape until you make a hole in their wall by eating the eggs there. Only the red snake is able to move about right away. As soon as the snakes are on the loose they start eating the eggs too and the player's character needs to avoid their heads. Their body also gets longer with each egg they eat and that way they can block the path. There is a strategy to it by keeping the snakes walled in as long as possible while avoiding the red snake.

The goal is to eat all the eggs so the second stage starts. It has different gameplay as now the goal is to eat the snakes by biting their tails. The game keeps track of the score and the high score is registered.

218300.overview:
During World War II a highly guarded compound has been photographed by a reconnaissance plane hidden in a forest. After many intelligent reports it has been discovered that under the compound is a research complex which is getting nearer to the development of a bacterial virus and a new type of rocket which when combined will cause devastation and disease. You and a team of four, have been tasked to parachute into the forest in the surrounding area of the compound to find it's location, then get in the compound before trying to enter the complex. Once in the compound you have to get the plans for the virus, rocket fuel and guidance system before finally blowing the place up. Once your mission has been completed you must then get to a rendezvous point to be picked up by a plane. Remember though, the surrounding areas have patrolling guards and the compound and complex are heavily guarded.

Before you start you can pick from seven missions where each one is more difficult than the last one. The first mission is just to find the compound and photograph it, while the last mission is where you have to actually blow up the complex and reach the rendezvous point. You then choose how long in hours (1-9 times ten) the mission will take before the plane arrives. Each movement in the forest is worth 20 minutes while inside the compound it is 2 minutes. Once you are happy with your selected options you must pick a team of four soldiers to attempt the mission with yourself. There are 30 skills to choose from in which you as the leader have all 30 but the other soldiers only have two of them. You are only aware of one skill for each soldier so you can interview each man to find the other skill or just select them. Each interview will take a day but you only have eight days before the mission starts.

Once you are happy with your selections you then start the game. You view the forest from above, with the whole forest shown on the screen. You cannot see any terrain but just the trees. You are shown as a flashing square and you can see any objects one place around you in the North, South, East and West positions. There are location's that can be found as you explore the area, and they are caves, potholes, lakes or houses. These can be explored for any equipment that might be left there and next to the map of the forest is a map of the location you want to explore. You can only see so far in front so you have to move around to see more of the location's passages. Any items found can be picked up. Occasionally in the forest you will come across a patrol and these will need killing. To the right of the forest map again is a map of the area you are in showing your men's positions and the positions of the patrol. You then select which enemy soldier any of your soldiers will shoot at then move your soldier selected two places. You fire at the patrol and then they fire back.

218303.overview: This is a collection of Lunar Lander style games, conserve your fuel and land on the platform below and, depending on the level, avoid different obstacles.

218304.overview:
Street Machine is a racing game where you have to race against seven computer controlled cars on a long street circuit for three laps. Each lap has different conditions with Lap One in the day, Lap Two at night and Lap Three in the snow. Before your race you can choose a coloured car before you go to the starting grid and ready for your race. The game is viewed from above and the screen shows a small part of the circuit with the screen scrolling in all directions as you drive. You push forward on the joystick to accelerate and press the fire button to brake. Points are awarded to the car leading after each lap and the winner is the car with the most points.

As you drive and try to overtake the other drivers care must be taken not to hit the other cars or the side of the road as this damages your car. Take to much damage during a lap and a maintenance chart appears with over 70 parts of your vehicle and what percentage of damage it has occurred. You have to change any damage to below 79% as a timer counts down. Fail to change all damage then it's race over. Hit a car or the side of the road too fast and the car can be too damaged to fix and it's race over there and then. If you manage to complete a lap then you have to fix your car to move on to the next lap.

218570.overview: Rod Hyde was always determined to produce the most realistic and advanced flight simulations ever, and this early attempt at recreating the Harrier is an example of that. There are 3 skill levels, as well as two practice modes - one for the rudiments of flight and the other for combat. The action-centered nature of the title means that it can be seen as an advanced shoot 'em up rather than a pukka flight simulator. Acquiring a lock on enemy planes and tanks is made easier by the advanced targeting technology of the planes, and escaping enemy fire is aided by the vectored thrust system. Shooting out the tanks clears ground space to set up your own bases, which must then be defended. VTOL (vertical take-off and landing) is correctly implemented, although more traditional horizontal take-offs should be used when space permits. The full range of weapons are provided; experience will tell you which to use in which situations, based on enemy volume and range.

419290.overview:
A game in which you play as a wizard and fight demons. To be successful you will need to transform at times into a torch, a cross or a magic ring.
You stand at the portals between this world and the astral world, surrounded by a pictogram of power.
The red magic boxes may be used to transform into a torch, a cross, a magic ring and back to a wizard.
As a torch you can light the candles. When all 4 are lit you can transform back to a wizard and do battle with the demon.
Transforming into a cross repels attacks.
The magic ring will restore your depleted energy, but it's elusive and is not always visible.
When a demon is destroyed you are ready to face the next one.

The game was supposed to be released by MRM Software, but the game got cancelled.

419831.overview:
You are in command of a Naval Frigate. Below you, numerous submarines lurk, intent on destroying you with anti-ship mines.
It is your job to protect your warship by eliminating the submarines using your proximity-depth charges.
Watch out for the Super Subs. These require a random number of hits to be destroyed. Also note that they are indistinguishable from other submarines.
Try to hit the deeper submarines as these are worth more points.

419841.overview: A homebrew take on Taito's Space Invaders.

419847.overview:
The object of the game is to protect the octopi from certain death from the sharks. You control a shark net and you have to surround as many octopi as you can with the net, to prevent the sharks getting to them. Beware of touching an octupus as it's poisonous.
If a shark manages to eat an octopus before you can protect it, the shark becomes a killer shark, which eats everything in its path, including your net.
After you have protected the octopi (or after they have all been eaten), you must fill the majority of the screen with the net to enable you to procede to the next screen.

419881.overview: Space Intruders is a clone of the popular arcade game Space Invaders for the BBC Micro, where the object is to navigate your ship left or right, using its built-in laser fire to destroy five rows of aliens who work their way down towards you. If any of these aliens make contact with the ship, a life will be lost. Four bases are there to protect your ship, but these bases can be destroyed piece by piece. From time to time, a UFO will make its way across the screen; and shooting it will award you with bonus points. The game ends when all lives have been lost.

420194.overview: A side -scrolling shooter. Referred to by it's short name of Scramble on the boxart spine, it was known by it's full title of Bomber Scramble in-game.

420666.overview:
Your spaceship is patrolling a sector of space where aliens are laying mines. Your task is to destroy the aliens whilst avoiding collision with them and the mines.
You have an unlimited fuel supply and can fire at any hostile object with your lasers. You will get 150 points for each alien you hit and 50 points for each mine. Each time you clear a screenful of aliens you are awarded an extra 1,000 points. At the start you have three ships but every time you score 10,000 points you gain another ship.

420669.overview:
An alien swamp is infested with monsters. You control a robot sent in to destroy them. The only way to do that is to move the stepping stones in the swamp so that the monsters will fall in and drown. However, the swamp monsters will try to destroy the robot first.
There are three kinds of monsters living on the surface and a fourth kind, the lake monster, which cannot be killed. The lake monsters are normally no trouble provided the robot keeps moving.
The red monsters are the least intelligent and are worth 100 points for each one your manage to drown. Yellow monsters are worth 200 points and white monsters 300 points. The white monsters may mutate into Lake Monsters when they fall in the water; the only way to prevent this is to drop a stone on them before the change starts. If you succeed, it is worth 500 points.
When you destroy one screenful, another will appear. The robot only has a limited power supply, how quickly this is used up depends on how many stones it is carrying. If it tries to carry more than two, then it will sink. You start off with three robots and will be given extra for each 5,000 points.

420717.overview: You are a professor in your laboratory. A potion you were mixing slips from your grasp and spills. A choking green fume overcomes you. A fuzzy sleep strikes you down. When you awake, to your horror you find that your body is less than one inch in height. The only way to regain your height is to get to the top of the lab table, where there are some crystals that will restore you.

420746.overview:
You are presented with a grid of letters which have been shuffled. Use your skill to arrange them alphabetically. You must move one letter at a time into the vacant square. See how quickly you can arrive at the final result.

This game requires a light pen which should be plugged into the computer's 'analogue in' port.

420748.overview:
Based on the well known game of "Battleships" this game enables you to take charge of your fleet. You are in command and your mission is to seek and destroy as many enemy submarines and battleships as you can.

This game requires a light pen which should be plugged into the computer's 'analogue in' port.

420758.overview:
A U.S. Gold Master Games label compilation of 4 games originally released as individual titles by Adventure International.

All 4 games are single player text adventures.

Buckaroo Banzai (aka The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai across the 8th Dimension): by Phillip Case, Kem McNair and Scott Adams. It was converted to the BBC Micro by Brian Howart and originally released in 1987. Fifteenth game in the Scott Adams Adventure series.

Pirate Adventure: by Scott and Alexis Adams. It was converted to the BBC Micro by Brian Howart and Cliff Ogden and originally released in 1984. Second game in the Scott Adams Adventure series.

Strange Odyssey: by Scott Adams. Two BBC Micro conversions were made; one by Mak Jukic and another by Brian Howart and Cliff Ogden, with both originally released in 1984. Sixth game in the Scott Adams Adventure series.

Voodoo Castle: by Scott and Alexis Adams. It was converted to the BBC Micro by Brian Howart and Cliff Ogden and originally released in 1984. Fourth game in the Scott Adams Adventure series.

421069.overview:
Your mission is to become the galactic ruler: explore neighbouring solar systems with your scout ships and evaluate your chances of success if you attack another planet.
The inhabitants may be primitive, atomic or sophisticated, so you must prepare your fleet for the final assault. The more systems you rule, the more powerful you become until finally you conquer the universe.

This game was initially published by Software For All for the BBC Model B and was followed within a very short interval by the Cosma release which was BBC A/B compatible.

421073.overview: A sword duelling game for 2 players.

421184.overview: A gallery space shooter, number 14 in the IJK Software Cassette series.

421236.overview:
Arena, known in-game as Space Arena, is a two player gallery space shooter.
This game was published on the cassette bundled with the Micro User magazine, volume 5, issue 8, of October 1987.

421293.overview:
A compilation of 8 games published in cassette and floppy disk formats, 7 of which were previously released as stand alone titles by Superior Software.
Syncron was a new release; a cassette version was later published on the Superior/Blue Ribbon budget label.

Airlift, a single player scrolling action rescue game by Peter Johnson (1984)
BMX on the Moon, a single player Moon Buggy style game by Tim Tyler and Ian Robinson (1984)
Karate Combat, a fighting game for up to 2 players by Martin Sykes (1986)
Repton, a single player scrolling maze game by Tim Tyler (1985)
Star Striker, a single player gallery space shooter by Jim Daniels (1984)
Smash and Grab, a single player platformer by Walter Mansell (1984)
Syncron, a single player scrolling shooter by Gary Partis (1987)
Wallaby, a single player platformer by Peter Johnson and David Lovekin (1984)

421303.overview:
A compilation of 8 single player games released on cassette and floppy disk formats. As with the first volume, it comprised 7 previously published titles as well as a new one (Kix) all by Superior Software.

Battle Tank, a scrolling shooter by Mark Silver (1983)
Crazy Painter (aka Amidar), a maze game by Adrian Stephens (1983)
Deathstar, a scrolling shooter by Peter Johnson (1985)
Kix, a Qix style avoid them game by Alwyn Adolf (1987)
Missile Strike, a gallery space shooter by Charles Robertson (1984)
Overdrive, a car driving game by Peter Johnson (1984)
Repton 2, a scrolling maze game by Tim Tyler (1985)
Space Pilot, a scrolling shooter by Peter Johnson and David Lovekin (1984)

421337.overview:
The primary objective of the game is to retrieve the Emperor's Stolen Lamp. This is an heirloom handed down since the days of Alaa Eldeen. In order to do this, you must survive many dangers and solve many problems. As a secondary objective, you must return with as much treasure as you can, and this will require as much cunning as the main quest.

The game was published by Lothlorien, and was also included in the Paxman Promotions' War Games Pack.

421443.overview: A  UK classroom favourite throughout the 80s and 90s, this graphical adventure game puts you in the role of an investigative reporter tracking down leads about the reclusive Charles Hinton.

421496.overview: A fruit machine simulation known as Super Fruits on the box and cassette, and as Super Fruit in-game.

421497.overview: Your plan is as follows. Launch successfully into orbit. Fetch a malfunctioning satellite by first parking next to it and then retrieving the device with your remote control arm. After the satellite is safely stored, close the bay doors, fire retros and begin re-entry. Fly into a final-approach window and perform a mock landing-flare. Then start your final approach to the runway resulting in a safe landing, debrief your mission afterwards to find your successful phases of flight, and your mission score compared to the high score.

421500.overview: A Fruit Machine simulation featuring sound, spinning reels, five row by four column display of fruit, win-line, "bounce" as each reel settles, nudge box, nudge, gambles, two way nudges, swap reels, hold reels, collect win, gamble win, "loser's gamble" if the first gamble is lost, super gamble for the jackpot, and a coin pile that shrinks and grows with your winnings.

421508.overview:
Your mission is to launch the Shuttle into space on a pre-set flight path. You must then orbit the earth to find two satellites, the first is from an enemy and will explode and destroy you, unless you destroy him with your laser first. Next, you must find your own N.A.S.A. satellite and with the Shuttle's remote-controlled arm bring it safely on board. The last, and perhaps most difficult, task now faces you, bringing your precious cargo safely back to earth.

You may choose to fly a complete mission as above, or to practise separate sections: Satellite attack, Satellite rescue, Manual landing.

421694.overview: You are in command of an Exploration Starship. Your mission, to explore and trade in five star systems. The Empire is at Advanced level of intelligence. It needs the resources of the Ultimate Computer. This can be obtained from the only super race in existence. Your aim is to obtain it and get it to Sol.

421875.overview:
Long ago Lord Sadim returned from the wars to find that his wife Leonora had been unfaithful and he had her sealed up in her room to die.
Many years later you visit the now deserted and haunted castle: your task is to locate Leonora's remains and give her a decent burial, thereby setting her vengeful spirit to rest.
Sadim Castle is a real-time adventure. This means the game will continue to play when it is waiting for you to enter a command and the characters you encounter may not wait for you to think.
The screen is split into two sections; the top part shows what is happening around you whilst the bottom section is reserved for your commands.

422115.overview: The year is 1910. You were sailing on an antiquated tramp steamer bound for Borneo, when there was an explosion in the engine room and the ship sank. Your objective is to reach the tropical island, survive it's perils and return to civilization, or to find eternal happiness.

422203.overview:
A Space Invaders variant for one or two players featuring 64 invaders and a flying saucer.
It was also released with the box title Invaders by PSS, although in-game it was still referred to as Secta Invaders.

424657.overview:
The object of the game is to repair the Srexis Grid.
The grid components are highly volatile and must be placed correctly and quickly, as, once out of their protective pod, they remain inactive for only a limited period before automatic assembly occurs.
The corner components are placed, then you must position the rest. No two similar components can be adjacent, as this would fuse the grid and terminate the Srexis.

425560.overview: A text adventure in which you take on the role of a policeman.

425579.overview:
A text adventure in which you reprise the role of Paul I Grace, a policeman.
The game is more of an alternative than a sequel to the original Street Patroller - it's a completely different game but shares the same basic plot as the original.

425801.overview:
A twin cassette compilation of 7 Software Invasion games which were originally released as standalone titles except for Street Machines which was a new title released for this compilation and advertised as such on the cover.

The compilation was also released on floppy disk.

3D Bomb Alley: a 1983 gallery shooter by Simon Vout.
Attack On Alpha Centauri: a 1983 gallery space shooter by Simon Vout.
Eagle's Wing: a 1984 scrolling shooter by Marcus Bott-Obi.
Gunsmoke: a 1984 gallery shooter by Simon Vout.
Spooks And Spiders: a 1984 platformer by S.R. and L.J. Whiting.
Street Machine: a 1986 top down driving game by Simon Vout.
Vortex: a 1983 gallery space shooter by Simon Vout.

438365.overview:
Subhunt is a complimentary game to Blockade. Here the roles are reversed and you are the captain of a destroyer seeking out and attacking an enemy submarine.

The two games were issued as separate titles for the BBC Micro, whereas they were titled "War at Sea" a single cassette compilation for the Electron.

438375.overview:
This is an adventure set in the world of spies and espionage.

Blue Ribbon re-released this game coupled with the game Banana Man as a double-pack.

438376.overview:
The object of this sequel to Secret Sam 1 is to obtain a top-secret document and escape without being caught.

The game was re-released by Blue Ribbon as a double-pack coupled with the game The Guy In The Hat.

439106.overview:
Try to remove all the pegs from the board leaving one peg in the centre.
You have to jump over a peg to move and you can't move diagonally.

439146.overview:
A Lunar Lander type game.

This was the feature game on the Micro User cassette, volume 3, issue 3.
It was also available to download from the BBC teletext service Ceefax in June 1988.

439204.overview:
Having secretly landed on Vadros, you must enter the Vader HQ.
Your mission is to locate the weapon's design, the attack plans and a Positronic robotic brain, and return them to Patrol HQ.

439818.overview:
Not to be confused with the Micro Power game of the same name.

This is a strategy cum spaceship management game with combat elements. You are the captain of the starship Enterprise with a mission to destroy all the Klingon warships in the Galaxy within a specified time.

It was also published by R.H. Software as part of a three game compendium.

448564.overview:
You control a battery of three bases which you must use to shoot the sharks that are swimming beneath the ships, threatening to surface and gouge a hole in their hulls.
Shooting the sharks is made more difficult by ocean currents which can easily change the direction of the missile sending it directly into one of the ships.

The game was written by Carl Robertshaw and appeared as a listing in the January 1985 issue of Computer and Video Games.

457159.overview: Choose from 6 different puzzles to slide the pieces into the vacant slot, opening up new opportunities to complete the puzzle. You can opt for between 2 automated moves from the original picture all the way up to 511!

457190.overview:
Bouncer is a 1-player arcade game for the BBC Micro.

The player controls a large circle of anti-matter while Space Bouncers jump about the screen. The player has to position the circle so that Space Bouncers land in the center of the circle and are destroyed. If the Space Bouncers are not perfectly centered, the anti-matter is destroyed. The player has a limited time to destroy all bouncers on the screen. If the player loses three lives, it's game over.

457192.overview: The Statix is a dangerous electrical charge which twists and turns unpredictably as it guards its territory. The player controls a character that can safely move around the boundary of the screen, but is vulnerable when moving onto the Statix's territory. The player tries to gain territory by cordoning off sections of the screen by drawing blocks, with the goal to gain 75% of the screen to move to the next level with a faster-moving Statix. The player must avoid sparks which follow the player, and fuses which chase the player if they draw new boundaries too slowly.

457215.overview:
The object of the game is to eat up the red snake segments that are spread randomly around the screen.  For every one eaten both the length of the snake and the score are increased by one and one purple segment will appear on the screen.  If these purple ones are eaten the score and the length are increased by two and one green block will appear.  If these are hit the snake is electrocuted.  The same fate awaits any snake that touches the edge of its cage.

The fire button will destroy anything within five squares in front of the snake, except for the cage wall, and decrease the score by one point.

457514.overview:
Shipwreck is a text adventure game in which players take the role of a sailor returning home from a successful voyage when disaster strikes. After the ship is damaged during a violent storm, the player must survive and find a way to safety, initially clinging to floating debris and eventually exploring a desert island.

The game is played entirely via text commands. Players input verbs and directions to move, collect items, solve puzzles, and interact with the environment. Abbreviations are supported, and basic inventory and status systems are included. The game tracks player progress, inventory capacity, and survival factors like thirst. Objects can be combined or used creatively to overcome obstacles—for instance, transforming a basket into a boat using tar. A magic word can influence events, and players can save or restore their position.

Shipwreck includes a time-based storm system and random events, such as encounters with a snake or a hostile island inhabitant. Navigation covers locations aboard the ship, underwater, and throughout a multi-zone island with beaches, cliffs, forests, and caves. The ultimate goal is to escape the island by delivering a valuable item to a ship’s captain offshore. 
 
Published on the Model B Computing cassette number 10 in April/May 1985.

457526.overview:
Sink the Bismarck is a naval strategy simulation game set during World War II. The player assumes the role of Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Navy in the North Atlantic, tasked with locating and sinking the German battleship Bismarck.

The game presents a top-down map of the North Atlantic, displaying the positions of British naval forces and the last known location of the Bismarck. Players issue orders to various ships, directing their movements and coordinating attacks. The gameplay involves strategic planning, as players must anticipate the Bismarck's movements and deploy their forces effectively to intercept and engage the enemy vessel.

Sink the Bismarck emphasizes strategic decision-making over real-time action. There is no direct control over individual ship combat; instead, success depends on effective allocation of resources and anticipation of enemy tactics. The game does not feature real-time graphics or animations, focusing instead on strategic map-based gameplay.

458357.overview:
SAS Commander is a single-player gallery-style shooter in which the player, acting as an SAS unit, receives mission coordinates and must scramble their squadron to intercept enemy targets. Gameplay involves selecting squadrons, navigating maps, and engaging incoming enemies in individual mission screens where timely key presses determine success or failure.

At the start of each mission, the player inputs a squadron number (1–9) following an alert prompt such as “SCRAMBLE…SCRAMBLE…”. A map displays the selected squadron's base, aircraft count, and status. The player then enters target coordinates to deploy fighters. The game transitions to a static combat screen: enemies appear, and the player presses designated keys to fire or avoid attacks. Success depends on accuracy and speed.

458359.overview:
Satan’s Challenge is a horror-themed text adventure about confronting occult forces threatening those closest to you. Also released under the title Nevil Rides Out, the game begins as the player arrives at a remote hamlet where dark powers are concentrated. A supernatural ceremony must be performed to summon and safely confront Lucifer, involving a ritual pentagram and specific items such as holy water, candles, and horseshoes.

The player assumes the role of a lone figure determined to halt a growing supernatural threat. After learning that loved ones are in danger, the protagonist travels to a deserted village where malevolent forces have gathered. The only way to stop the evil is to summon Lucifer using a partially understood magical rite. The final confrontation can only occur safely if the correct elements are assembled and the ritual completed. As the game begins, environmental obstacles—such as a flood cutting off escape—already suggest that the opposing forces are actively working to stop you.

Players input typed commands using a standard verb–noun parser (e.g., “GO NORTH”, “USE CANDLE”). The adventure consists of exploring locations, examining items, and piecing together the required steps of the ritual while avoiding or overcoming supernatural threats. Navigation and object usage are critical, and hints are conveyed through environmental text.

458380.overview: Sea Wolf has players command a nuclear sub attempting to destroy enemy ships and targets on screen. Players navigate using keyboard commands to control torpedoes and sub movement, aiming at surface vessels. Each level presents static screens depicting enemy ships; the player must engage and sink them for points.

459202.overview: Jump in the fast lane in some of Scotland's most scenic railways. Control the speed and the signals and manage all the freight and passengers to make the most money, have the least issues and meet the schedules.
